did_you_know.text: Did you know? In chapter 8, wisdom and understanding are portrayed as figures calling out and inviting people to listen to them.
Did you know? Wisdom does not hide; she calls out beside the city gates, at the entrances, and in the public places where people pass by.
Did you know? Wisdom also addresses the simple and the foolish, encouraging them to gain prudence, understanding, and a discerning heart.
Did you know? The chapter places instruction and knowledge above silver and gold, presenting the words of wisdom as an especially precious treasure.
Did you know? According to the chapter, the fear of the LORD is connected with hating evil, pride, arrogance, an evil way, and perverse speech.
Did you know? Wisdom is presented as the foundation of just leadership: through it kings reign and rulers make laws of justice.
Did you know? Wisdom promises that those who love her will be loved in return, and that those who diligently seek her will find her.
Did you know? Beginning in verse 22, wisdom is described as existing before the creation of the world—before the depths, the mountains, the earth, and the dust of the world.
Did you know? Wisdom is described as being present when the heavens were prepared, the boundaries of the sea and the deep were set, and the foundations of the earth were established.
Did you know? The chapter concludes by presenting listening to wisdom and following her ways as the path to life and to finding favor with the LORD, while rejecting her harms oneself.
